anatomy.note: This site's picture of where the kinds of firm on this page are heading. It is a model of an idea, joined from the arguments on the page before; no reading tests it whole.

parts.does: Set the task, sign the work, hold the licence, face the customer, and pay when it is wrong. Few, senior, and named.
parts.name: The people who answer

parts.does: Tests, reviewers and records that settle whether work was done right. Where no check exists, a person's judgement stands in, and this is where most work waits.
parts.name: The checking layer

parts.does: Agents now; agents that keep context next; robots later. Wide, cheap, and not employed.
parts.name: The working base

parts.does: The models themselves, bought by the token from whoever sells them cheapest.
parts.name: Rented

parts.does: What cannot be bought: customers, the firm's records and context, its licences, its sensors and sites.
parts.name: Owned

anatomy.title: The anatomy of an AI-run firm

kinds.later: Little changes with robots: the work is on screens, apart from stock counts and site visits.
kinds.name: Accounting practice
kinds.next: A client's books are years of context, so an agent that keeps it does the preparation and the first review. The practice becomes reviewers and client partners, with few preparers and few trainees.
kinds.now: Buyers built around AI own these firms more than sell to them, and this is the trade with the most of them. One group reports a tax pilot that cut preparation time and says it does not expect to need fewer accountants. One bookkeeping firm says its software closes the books with no person involved and logs every step. Every figure is the operators' own.
kinds.signs: A licensed accountant for audits and reviews; the firm's own reviewer for tax returns and books
titles: Accounting, Tax Preparation, Bookkeeping, and Payroll Services
kinds.wrong: A roll-up reporting, after a full tax season, revenue per person no higher than ordinary firms; or a state board disciplining a firm over audit work an agent prepared.

kinds.later: Robots do not bear on it.
kinds.name: Law firm
kinds.next: A firm's precedents and each client's history are held by the agent. Leverage turns over: fewer associates under each partner, and more matters for each lawyer who signs.
kinds.now: The census passes almost none of a lawyer's own work, and courts keep finding filings with invented citations. New firms are built with agents drafting and lawyers reviewing everything. England's regulator has licensed one firm run on AI for small debt claims, on conditions: it may not propose case law, the client approves each step, and named solicitors answer for the output.
kinds.signs: A named lawyer on every piece of work; outside a few places, only lawyers may own the firm
kinds.wrong: A large firm publishing steady hiring of junior lawyers after years of agent use; or firms owned by non-lawyers failing to grow where they are allowed.

kinds.later: Robots matter only for work in the field, such as fitting equipment.
kinds.name: Software and IT services company
kinds.next: Agents hold the codebase and its history. Engineers specify, review and answer; managers who relayed information thin out; the junior rung is the open question.
kinds.now: The trade furthest along, because tests are a check everyone accepts. One large company says AI writes a sizeable share of its new code, which engineers then review. A randomised trial found experienced developers slower with AI while believing themselves faster. The largest outsourcers employ fewer people than a year ago, in a weak market as well.
kinds.signs: The engineer who reviews and accepts the change; no licence
titles: Computer Systems Design and Related Services
kinds.wrong: A repeat of the trial with current tools still finding a slowdown; or the outsourcers' headcount recovering as demand does.

kinds.later: Branches and cash are the only physical part, and they are already shrinking for other reasons.
kinds.name: Bank or lender
kinds.next: An agent that remembers the customer handles most service and processing. People sit in risk, exceptions and the decisions an examiner will ask about.
kinds.now: Agents are in service and operations, not in deciding who gets credit. One bank projected fewer people in operations; two lenders that cut service staff for a chatbot took people back. In April the American bank regulators rewrote their rules for models and left agents out of them, so a bank has no approved way to show an examiner that an agent is under control.
kinds.signs: The bank's own risk function, and a registered supervisor for anything sold as advice
titles: Credit Intermediation and Related Activities (5221 and 5223 only)
kinds.wrong: The regulators extending the old model rules to agents unchanged; or the banks that took people back finding they need few.

kinds.later: Robots or drones inspect damage; repair stays with other trades.
kinds.name: Insurer or insurance broker
kinds.next: Software takes in a claim, checks it and pays it. People remain for refusals, disputes and large or strange risks, and for selling to businesses.
kinds.now: One insurer built on AI grew its premiums far faster than its staff and says it spends much less than rivals on handling claims, while still losing money. Two American states have bills that leave sorting, fraud scoring and approvals to software and require a person only to refuse a claim. On brokers this site found almost nothing.
kinds.signs: A licensed adjuster or agent; under bills now proposed, a person for any refusal to pay
titles: Agencies, Brokerages, and Other Insurance Related Activities
kinds.wrong: That insurer's staff growing in step with its premiums; or the bills on refusals failing.

kinds.later: This is where robots would matter most and are furthest off: bodies are fragile, and the work the census cannot see is most of a hospital.
kinds.name: Hospital or medical practice
kinds.next: An agent holding the patient's whole record drafts, orders and follows up routine care. Clinicians examine, decide and sign, each for more patients; the office behind them thins.
kinds.now: What has spread is note-taking: software that writes up the visit. Clinicians report less burnout; an independent review finds no clear saving. One American state lets a company renew routine prescriptions without a doctor signing, after doctors reviewed its first decisions, with insurance that covers the software. The state's own medical board asked for a halt and was refused.
kinds.signs: A licensed clinician, everywhere but one state's trial
kinds.wrong: Harm in that state's trial, or other states copying it quickly; or a controlled trial finding note-taking software does nothing for burnout.

kinds.later: Agency work that is physical, such as warehouse shifts, goes the way of the warehouses.
kinds.name: Staffing and business-support firm
kinds.next: An agent that remembers each customer and learns from corrections takes first contact. The firm sells results, not seats, and keeps a small team for the cases that escalate.
kinds.now: The trade with the most figures and the most reversals. One software company says it runs support with far fewer people. The large contact-centre operators report flat or falling revenue. The one careful study found an assistant made agents faster, novices most. Firms that removed people too quickly brought some back. For staffing agencies themselves there are targets and little else.
kinds.signs: Nobody by law; the customer who expects a person
kinds.wrong: The large operators' revenue recovering; or the companies that cut support staff quietly hiring them back.

kinds.later: Robots do not bear on it.
kinds.name: Management consultancy
kinds.next: Research, analysis and drafts come from agents that hold the firm's past work. Fewer, more senior people sell, frame the question and stand behind the answer.
kinds.now: The evidence is thin and mostly second-hand. What is on record is a failure: a large firm repaid part of a government fee after its report was found to cite things that did not exist. There is no licence and no accepted check for advice, so the client cannot verify it and reputation carries the sale.
kinds.signs: A partner, on the firm's name alone
titles: Management, Scientific, and Technical Consulting Services
kinds.wrong: A leading firm publishing its headcount by level and showing junior intake holding steady.

kinds.later: Of the service trades this is the one robots change most, through maintenance, and there is no evidence of it yet.
kinds.name: Property manager or estate agent
kinds.next: Software that knows each building and tenant runs the tenancy. People win landlords, handle disputes and hold the client money.
kinds.now: The clearest roll-up case. One British buyer of letting agencies says each of its staff handles several times the usual number of homes, with software doing messages, rent and the arranging of repairs; its investor says margins rose where the software is fully in use. Both are the company's own account. The physical part, repairs and viewings, is still people.
kinds.signs: The agent who holds clients' money; licensing varies by place
kinds.wrong: An independent count putting that buyer's homes per person near the ordinary level; or complaints rising at the agencies it bought.

kinds.later: The trade robots reach first: fixed routes and warehouses now, general handling later. The yard and the road are where the firm changes most.
kinds.name: Freight and logistics operator
kinds.next: Quoting, booking and tracking run without people. The broker's office becomes a small desk for exceptions and customers.
kinds.now: Most of the payroll here is not office work, so the census sees little of it. In the office part, the largest American freight broker reports each person handling many more shipments than a few years ago, a company measure that mixes AI with other changes. Driverless trucks are hauling freight on fixed routes, and one retailer counts its warehouse robots in very large numbers.
kinds.wrong: The broker's gain reversing when freight volumes recover; or the driverless operator missing its fleet target.

kinds.later: The kind of firm most exposed to robots and least sure of the date. One carmaker plans humanoids on a line within a few years; a veteran roboticist expects hands to stay far short of human ones for a decade.
kinds.name: Manufacturer
kinds.next: Planning, purchasing and scheduling are run by agents that know the plant. Engineers and managers remain; clerical work thins.
kinds.now: This site found almost nothing on agents in a manufacturer's offices, and says so. On the floor the base is ordinary industrial robots, installed in large numbers every year. The best-documented humanoid trial is a single task at a single car plant, since retired.
kinds.signs: Whoever answers for product safety and for the workers beside the machines
kinds.wrong: A carmaker publishing a humanoid's cost per task below a worker's; or the dated plan slipping.

kinds.later: Warehouses first, as in freight. The shop floor changes last, because shoppers are there.
kinds.name: Retailer
kinds.next: Agents buy, price and plan stock within limits a person sets. Head office thins; the shop floor does not.
kinds.now: The largest retailer says its headcount will stay flat while the work changes. An AI model set to run a small shop lost money and invented a payment account. Two physical experiments were withdrawn: checkout without cashiers, and robots that scanned shelves.
kinds.signs: The store operator; pharmacy and alcohol aside, no licence
titles: Food and Beverage Retailers (4451 and 4452 only)
kinds.wrong: The largest retailer's headcount falling well before the decade ends; or a repeat of the shop experiment turning a profit unaided.

stages.name: Now
stages.rests_on: What operators and regulators have published, and this site's census. Most operator figures are their own.

stages.name: Next
stages.rests_on: Judgement. Models cannot yet be taught on the job; the writers this site reads date it from late in this decade to well into the next.
stages.what: Agents that keep context and learn on the job

stages.name: Later
stages.rests_on: Extrapolation. The evidence is a few trials and plans; bank forecasts put the real rise late in the next decade, and a veteran roboticist later still.
stages.what: Robots that do physical work with that context
